The existing same-message MODIFY captures the copied-and-scaled options but leaves two stale constraints prohibiting the Hero V expressive right-arm geometry in the second V, which conflicts with copying the approved Hero V as a whole.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for restoring the foundation. I think we're much closer now.

Before we continue refining the alphabet, I'd like to revisit one aspect of the VvÉ system. Looking back at our earlier explorations, I prefer the hierarchy between the Hero V and the second V in concepts #2 and #3 (attached). I don't think the current proof has quite achieved that same relationship yet.

Will you please show these two options?

Option 1: Create the second V by copying the approved Hero V and reducing it proportionally as a single object (without redrawing it). It should remain a true scaled version of the Hero V while still extending above the E and L.

Option 2: Start with that same copied-and-scaled Hero V, then make only the minimal optical refinements you feel are necessary so it integrates more naturally with the alphabet while preserving the same identity and maintaining its elevation above the E and L.

Next, will you please refine the optical spacing throughout the word? I like the visual rhythm of the L–V relationship in this proof and would use that as the benchmark for balancing the remaining letter pairs.

I've attached the earlier concepts as a reference for the Hero V/second V relationship I'm referring to.

Thank you!

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY records concepts #2 and #3 as the preferred hierarchy reference, while the established elevation above E and L remains unchanged.
The approved Hero V remains the unchanged source geometry; the requested alternatives modify only how the second V is derived from it.
The source does not alter the required peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
The source reopens only the second V treatment and does not change the locked literal derivation of the É accent from the Hero V terminal.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records the L–V visual rhythm as the benchmark for optically balancing the remaining letter pairs.
The requested second-V options and optical-spacing refinement do not change the obligation to explain design intentions with review rounds.
The source concerns black-and-white glyph geometry and spacing and does not resume or modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
